title: From question to answer: what happens inside an AI model
performance: when an AI assistant gives them an answer at work, the viewer can explain how it was produced (predicted a piece at a time from the text in front of the model) and decide which claims to check before relying on them, and give the assistant the context it needs

audience.assumed_prior: uses or has seen a chat assistant; knows nothing of tokens, attention or sampling
audience.why: brief: non-technical corporate employees; the knowledge sheet explains every term in plain words
audience.motivation: wants to trust the tool the right amount and not be embarrassed by a wrong answer passed on
audience.context: desk or laptop, with sound, captions on, short workplace learning slot

strategy.name: question_led
strategy.rationale: the topic has a genuine puzzle at its heart (same question, two confident answers, one wrong) and the knowledge sheet's mechanism (F1-F17) answers it step by step in pipeline order
strategy.signature_move: ask what happens next to Priya's question, show that step happen on her words, then name it and say what it explains

misconceptions.belief: the assistant looks the answer up somewhere, like a search or a database
misconceptions.why_tempting: the reply arrives instantly and reads like a looked-up fact
misconceptions.source_anchor: knowledge F14, F15; not_claimed[0]; brief through_line

misconceptions.belief: an answer that sounds confident and well written is probably right
misconceptions.why_tempting: with people, fluency and confidence usually signal knowledge

hook.sketch: Say Priya asks the company assistant when expense claims are due, then asks again. She gets thirty days, then sixty, both said with total confidence.

arc.promise: follow Priya's one question through the model and you will know where each answer came from, and which to trust
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 opens from what the viewer already does: typing a question into a chat box

sections.goal: the viewer can explain how a typed question becomes tokens that the model weighs against each other
the viewer can use the predict, pick, append, repeat loop to explain why the same question gave two different answers
the viewer can distinguish an answer the model could ground in text it was given from one that is only a likely-sounding prediction, and say which needs checking

arc.payoff: back to Priya: neither number came from her policy; she pastes the policy in, asks again, and checks the date against the document before sharing it

practice_ladder.what: Priya's question traced through tokens, weights and the first predicted words, every step narrated
the ranked list for the deadline number is shown and the viewer is asked which pick explains thirty and which sixty before it is said
the viewer judges which of two replies needs checking, then sees Priya do it

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: So far the model has no answer, only Priya's pieces and how much each one matters. Keep that in mind.
Two replies: one summarises the policy Priya pasted in; one gives a deadline with no policy in front of the model. Which do you check first?
recall_moments.answer: the deadline with no policy in front of it: nothing in the context supported that number, so it is only a likely-sounding prediction
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: trusting the one that sounds more certain; confidence is written the same way for true and false statements (F16), and even the summary deserves a glance on key details

transfer_tasks: next time you ask an assistant something at work, paste in the document it should rely on, and check any name, figure, date or policy detail against the source before you pass it on

persona.voice: a calm, capable colleague who explains how the tool works without hype or alarm
persona.delivery_notes: curious and light on the hook, slower and even on attention, a beat of pause before the two answers split, plain and practical on the quiz and payoff

gagne.objective: promise: know where each answer came from and which to trust
gagne.recall_prior: sec1 starts from typing a question in a chat box
gagne.present: sections in pipeline order: tokens and weights, prediction loop, why it can be wrong
gagne.guidance: signature move applied to Priya's one question in every section
gagne.practice: faded prediction at sec2 end; quiz after sec3
gagne.feedback: quiz answer explained with the tempting wrong reading
gagne.transfer: transfer task: paste the source, check figures

merrill.problem_centered: Priya's deadline question is the running problem
merrill.activation: sec1 bridges from the viewer's own chat habit
merrill.demonstration: each step shown on Priya's words before it is named
merrill.application: faded prediction in sec2 and the sec3 quiz
merrill.integration: payoff and transfer task hand the habit back to the viewer's work

mayer.coherence: one running example only; no model sizes, vendors or history
mayer.redundancy: screen shows the tokens, weights and ranked words; narration explains, captions carry the words
mayer.contiguity: each token, weight and candidate word appears as it is spoken
mayer.segmenting: three short sections, one idea each
mayer.pre_training: token named in sec1 before the loop uses it in sec2

arcs.attention: two confident, different answers to one work question
arcs.relevance: the viewer's own use of assistants at work
arcs.confidence: every step shown on one familiar example before the quiz
arcs.satisfaction: the viewer resolves Priya's puzzle and knows what to do
